problem: The complete full-document BM25 index retrieved zero of seven persistent misses at generated-query top-20, and the preregistered passage BM25 representation recovered only two of seven against a four-case gate despite complete source and gold-document coverage.
simplest_baseline: Keep the identical 48 recorded successful queries and inspect the already pinned Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B index at fixed depths; do not generate queries, add a reranker, add agents, or run an end-to-end arm.
hypothesis: The fixed dense retriever places a gold document within top-100 for at least four of the seven persistent misses even if top-20 remains insufficient, which would localize the next problem to bounded candidate selection rather than query generation or corpus absence.
changed_mechanisms: offline retrieval scoring changed from frozen lexical ranks to the existing pinned dense semantic index
anti_claim: A dense gold-rank result on outcome-selected failures is diagnostic only and cannot be reported as a harness accuracy gain or model capability improvement.

framework_comparisons.current_gap: More workers cannot repair a shared candidate generator whose relevant documents remain below every worker's visible depth.
A configurable backend is useful only after the rank audit identifies whether the existing semantic backend has a viable candidate pool.
The cheapest remaining uncertainty is candidate depth for already generated queries, not another paid planning or crawling call.
Graph expansion targets branch omission; this audit first tests semantic rank under each existing branch query.

frozen_controls: same seven outcome-selected persistent retrieval misses
same trial-1 set and order of 48 successful generated queries
four byte-verified Tevatron dense index shards
query prefix, EOS pooling, normalization, and max length 512 from the pinned retriever manifest
zero provider, online search, and Judge calls
next_action: Implement the frozen dense-rank contract, reproduce the same 48 query hashes, and report per-case best gold ranks plus top-20, top-100, and top-1000 gates without changing the model or candidate depth after observation.
claim_boundary: The dense audit is CPU-only and gold-aware. A top-20 pass selects a retrieval candidate; a top-100-only pass selects another bounded offline reranking question; neither authorizes a fresh or official effectiveness claim by itself.
